correctness.rationale: Scaling reduces the weighted perimeter to \(r^{n-1+p}\) times a continuous spherical Riesz average. The radial Laplacian sign gives decreasing averages for Newtonian-through-zero negative powers, whereas subharmonicity treats nonnegative powers; an exterior derivative proves increasing perimeter for \(r<|c|\) when the power is subcritical. The singular cap integral makes the derivative infinite with opposite sign immediately after \(r=|c|\). Both one-sided cusp coefficients are derived from a convergent beta integral, with offset cancellation. All quantifiers, contact integrability, dimension 2, centered case and critical Newtonian equality are addressed. Supplementary script executed and passed 71 finite checks.

value.rationale: The sharp geometric dichotomy explains when nested translated balls maintain monotone negative-power weighted surface area; the threshold is exactly the Newtonian exponent and the failure occurs by singular contact. An explicit positive gamma coefficient gives a universal offset-invariant cusp and its exact optimal Hölder exponent for each \(n,p\). This supplies a motivated boundary example for recently studied weighted perimeters beyond a routine centered-ball calculation; it does not solve arbitrary convex inclusions.
